explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/805 (Erdős–Hajnal): 'For which functions g(n) with n > g(n) ≥ (log n)² is there a graph on n vertices in which every induced subgraph on g(n) vertices contains a clique of size ≥ log n and an independent set of size ≥ log n?'. In Lean IsLocallyRamsey G m k says every m-set of vertices contains a clique and an independent set of size ≥ k, HasRamseyGraphs g asks for such a graph with m = g n and k = ⌈log n⌉ for all large n, and the value question equates the set of g with (log n)² ≤ g n < n eventually and HasRamseyGraphs g to an answer set. Requiring the conditions for all large n is the natural asymptotic reading and is documented. Faithful encoding of a 'for which functions' question in the upstream answer-set style.
